run.engine: SciPy least_squares and deterministic cluster bootstrap

source.assay: hIR-A affinity relative to human insulin; 1.5% HSA

model.baseline: b_i is the measured 0 mmol/L value for experiment i; it is fixed, not fitted.
model.upper_response: T_i is fitted separately for each independent experiment.
model.fit_method: Unweighted nonlinear least squares on the 15 experiment-level source values; the zero-glucose values define the fixed baselines.

cluster_bootstrap.method: Resample the three independent experiments with replacement; refit experiment-specific upper responses and shared EC50/Hill slope for each sample.

interpretation.summary: The fitted midpoint varies widely when the three independent experiments are resampled. Some fits hit the 1000 mmol/L EC50 optimization ceiling, so the upper bootstrap tail is censored and no reliable midpoint interval is identified.
limits: Only three independent experiment clusters and five glucose concentrations are available.
The observed data do not establish a high-glucose response plateau; EC50 and upper response are therefore strongly correlated.
Bootstrap percentile ranges are fragile with three clusters and are not formal inferential confidence intervals.
The apparent Hill coefficient is a descriptive steepness parameter, not a binding-site count or proof of cooperativity.
No 6 mmol/L activation threshold is inferred; the secondary product-design target remains separate.
This fit describes published receptor-affinity data; it is not a molecular simulation, clinical model, or dosing recommendation.
